QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_57

question.text: For an open-ended Cat III AIF with called capital INR 50 cr, NAV (pre-incentives) at end of Y2 INR 63.2995 cr, HWM INR 56.42 cr, Reference Hurdle INR 60.50 cr, incentive fee rate 15%. Compute the incentive fee expressed to FOUR decimal places in INR crore:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ex 9.3: Minimum NAV eligible for incentive = higher of (HWM 56.42, Hurdle 60.50) = 60.50 cr. Excess = 63.2995 - 60.50 = 2.7995 cr. Incentive = 15% x 2.7995 = INR 0.4199 cr (i.e. INR 41,99,250). The stem asks for the answer to four decimal places, so 0.4199 is the uniquely correct value. The Trap: Option A (INR 2.7995 cr) is the excess amount itself before the 15% rate is applied. Option C (INR 0.9495 cr) uses HWM as the threshold instead of the higher of HWM/Hurdle. Option D is a fabricated distractor. The original item also offered INR 0.42 crore as a rounded distractor; because both 0.4199 and 0.42 were defensible rounded answers, that distractor created answer ambiguity and has been replaced. Note: The original item allowed two valid rounded answers (INR 0.4199 cr and INR 0.42 cr). The stem now specifies four-decimal precision and option D has been replaced with a materially different incorrect value so the keyed answer is uniquely correct. Source: FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 157-158.
